items.name: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.description: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. items.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
items.description: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. items.name: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
items.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
items.description: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. items.name: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
items.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
items.description: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. items.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
items.description: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. items.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
items.description: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique

items.name: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
items.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
items.description: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. items.name: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
items.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
items.description: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). items.name: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
items.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
items.description: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. items.name: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
items.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
items.description: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. items.name: Dexterity from Supervised Play
items.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
items.description: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. items.name: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
items.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
items.description: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. items.name: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
items.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
items.description: We develop a robust reinforcement learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes. items.name: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. items.name: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
items.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
items.description: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. items.name: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.description: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalizati

items.name: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
items.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
items.description: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. items.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
items.description: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. items.name: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
items.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
items.description: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. items.name: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
items.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
items.description: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. items.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
items.description: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. items.name: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
items.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
items.description: We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. items.name: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
items.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. items.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
items.description: With people increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, the need to evaluate these tools is becoming more pressing. Recent benchmarks attempt to mimic a realistic setting by simulating multi-turn interactions with synthetic patients and evaluating them with an LLM-as-a-judge. items.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
items.description: Spatial instructions describe how to move objects, transform regions, or modify their surroundings. When several operations are applied in sequence, each acts on a configuration shaped by earlier changes. How accurately can large language models (LLMs) predict the resulting spatial state? items.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
items.description: Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task. items.name: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
items.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe. items.name: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
items.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
items.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by querying external structured knowledge. However, it can also introduce privacy risks by leaking sensitive information from the retrieval datastore.
